description: Gradient fills at a starved bitrate, with nothing on disk. Behind everything, a colour asset painted with a radial gradient — lighter indigo a little above the middle, falling to near-black at the edges, the usual motion-graphics backdrop. Top right, an ellipse filled with a radial gradient from opaque yellow to fully transparent, so the backdrop shows through its rim with no grey fringe (the stops are interpolated premultiplied). Bottom centre, a pill with a white border whose fill runs left to right (angle 90) from orange, held flat for the first fifth by a repeated stop, to violet at the right end — measured across the pill's own box, so orange starts at its left end and not at the frame's left edge. Rendered at 60k, a starved bitrate, because that is where an undithered gradient bands: with the dither switched off (DITHER = 0 in crates/compositor/src/gradient.rs) this fixture fails at worst-block SSIM 0.81 on frame 0 and 0.88 on frame 29, the band edges being structure the encoder keeps. crates/render/tests/pipeline/banding.rs measures the same thing directly, as row-to-row jumps in luma. Frame 0 is x264's opening key frame at a coarse quantiser; frame 29 is the settled picture. What a wrong render looks like: a flat backdrop means a gradient on a color asset was read as one colour; violet on the left or orange across the whole pill means the angle is backwards or measured against the frame; a grey halo round the yellow ellipse means straight rather than premultiplied interpolation; a square yellow patch means the fill ignored the ellipse's outline.
